name: smart-folding
description: WebStorm-like code folding UX for VS Code: a bigger, highlighted, clickable '···' badge on folded blocks and single-line folds that hide the closing bracket.

commands.title: Expand Folded Block on This Line
Smart Unfold — Expand Parents at Remembered Cursor
Smart Unfold Recursively — Expand Parents + Children at Remembered Cursor

smartFolding.enhancedEllipsis.markdownDescription: Show a **bigger, highlighted `···` badge** at the end of every folded block (WebStorm style). Its background color comes from `#smartFolding.ellipsisBackground#` (default `#46494e`, the WebStorm badge color), giving a much larger visual target than VS Code's tiny ellipsis. Hovering it shows an **Expand** link, and with `#smartFolding.clickToExpand#` enabled, clicking next to it expands the block.

smartFolding.ellipsisBackground.markdownDescription: Background color of the `···` badge shown on folded blocks. Accepts any CSS color (e.g. `#46494e`, `rgba(83, 127, 231, 0.35)`). Leave **empty** to use the theme's selection color (`editor.selectionBackground`) instead.

smartFolding.ellipsisColor.markdownDescription: Text color of the `···` badge shown on folded blocks, for BOTH themes unless a theme-specific setting overrides it. Accepts any CSS color. Leave **empty** to use the theme's foreground color (`editor.foreground`) instead.

smartFolding.ellipsisBackgroundDark.markdownDescription: Background color of the `···` badge in **dark themes** (any CSS color, e.g. `#46494e`). Overrides `#smartFolding.ellipsisBackground#` when set; leave **empty** to fall back to it (and, if that is empty too, to the theme's `editor.selectionBackground`).

smartFolding.ellipsisBackgroundLight.markdownDescription: Background color of the `···` badge in **light themes** (any CSS color, e.g. `#dfe1e5`, the IntelliJ Light chip color). Overrides `#smartFolding.ellipsisBackground#` when set; leave **empty** to fall back to it (and, if that is empty too, to the theme's `editor.selectionBackground`).

smartFolding.ellipsisColorDark.markdownDescription: Text color of the `···` badge in **dark themes** (any CSS color). Overrides `#smartFolding.ellipsisColor#` when set; leave **empty** to fall back to it (and, if that is empty too, to the theme's `editor.foreground`).

smartFolding.ellipsisColorLight.markdownDescription: Text color of the `···` badge in **light themes** (any CSS color). Overrides `#smartFolding.ellipsisColor#` when set; leave **empty** to fall back to it (and, if that is empty too, to the theme's `editor.foreground`).

smartFolding.clickToExpand.markdownDescription: Expand a folded block when you **click at the end of its first line** (i.e. on/next to the `···` badge). This emulates WebStorm's large clickable ellipsis — the VS Code API does not allow making a decoration itself clickable, so the whole area after the code on a folded line becomes the click target.

smartFolding.clickLineToExpand.markdownDescription: Expand a collapsed block when you **click anywhere on its folded line** — on the code before the `···` badge too, not just on/next to the badge itself. Note: placing the cursor on a collapsed header line *without* expanding it becomes impossible, which is why this is off by default. Requires `#smartFolding.clickToExpand#`.

smartFolding.copyFoldedBlocks.markdownDescription: **Copying a collapsed block copies the WHOLE block**, hidden lines included. `Ctrl+C`/`Cmd+C` with the cursor on a collapsed line copies the entire folded block, and a selection that reaches the end of the collapsed row (`Shift+End`, a mouse drag up to the `···` badge) is widened through the hidden lines — with single-line folding the closing bracket is hidden too, so a plain copy of the visible row would paste broken code. Every other copy keeps VS Code's built-in behavior untouched.

smartFolding.modifierClickExpandsRecursi.markdownDescription: **Modifier+click on a fold badge expands the block RECURSIVELY** (folded descendants included). The modifier is VS Code’s multi-cursor modifier — `Alt` by default; set `#editor.multiCursorModifier#` to `ctrlCmd` to use `Ctrl`/`Cmd`+click instead. (VS Code does not report other modifier combinations such as `Alt+Shift` on mouse clicks, so only the multi-cursor modifier can be detected.)

smartFolding.takeOverFolding.markdownDescription: Be the sole folding provider for the configured languages (unified model verified against the tsserver parity suite + WebStorm single-line folds). Sets `#editor.defaultFoldingRangeProvider#` to `seymi.smart-folding` (only when you have not already pointed it at another provider yourself). **C, C++, C#, Java and PHP are excluded** from takeover — native folding remains active for them.

smartFolding.rememberCursorOnFoldAll.markdownDescription: **Fold All remembers your place.** When a fold swallows the cursor's line, VS Code jumps the cursor up to the fold header — this extension detects that jump and remembers the exact pre-fold position (line **and** column) per file, no matter HOW the fold was made (this extension's *Fold All* `Ctrl+K Ctrl+0`, the built-in Fold All, gutter fold icons, fold-level commands…). Running *Unfold All* (`Ctrl+K Ctrl+J`) restores the cursor to that exact spot and scrolls the view back to it — e.g. if you were at line 300, column 24, you land right back there. Disable to keep VS Code's default behavior.

smartFolding.smartUnfold.markdownDescription: **Smart Unfold (focus mode).** After a *Fold All*, unfolding at the remembered cursor expands ONLY the chain of parent blocks around it — from the top level down to the block the cursor is in — while every unrelated function/if/block stays collapsed. The cursor returns to its exact line & column and the view scrolls there. This kicks in (1) automatically for WHATEVER shortcut your keymap binds to the built-in unfold commands (via `#smartFolding.restoreOnAnyUnfold#`), and (2) via the `Smart Folding: Smart Unfold` / `Smart Unfold Recursively` commands in the Command Palette (bind your own keys to them if you like). Great for focusing on one piece of code.

smartFolding.restoreOnAnyUnfold.markdownDescription: **Restore the cursor after ANY unfold — whatever shortcut ran it.** This extension contributes no fold/unfold keybindings: while the cursor is still parked where a Fold All clamped it, any unfold that frees the remembered line (Unfold All, Unfold Recursively, a plain Unfold, a gutter chevron click — with any keymap) puts the cursor back at its exact line & column. Detection is self-verifying, so it works regardless of scroll position or where in the file the cursor was.

smartFolding.singleLineFolding.markdownDescription: **WebStorm behavior (default):** folding a block collapses it into a **single line** — the closing bracket line is folded away too (`function foo() {···`). **When disabled:** VS Code default — the closing bracket stays visible on its own line below the fold. Re-fold (Ctrl+Shift+[) after changing this setting; already-computed folds refresh on the next folding request.

smartFolding.foldComments.markdownDescription: **Fold comments.** Multi-line block comments / JSDoc — and runs of consecutive whole-line `//` comments — fold down to a readable one-line badge. Single-line comments like `/* one liner */` or a lone `//` line never fold.

smartFolding.commentPreview.markdownDescription: **Readable comment folds (WebStorm style).** A collapsed comment — its `/**` header included — collapses entirely into the gray badge, which shows the first meaningful text line instead of a plain ellipsis: `/** Remembers the cursor position when folding… */`.

smartFolding.commentPreviewLength.markdownDescription: Maximum characters of the collapsed-comment preview text (see `#smartFolding.commentPreview#`).

smartFolding.hideOpeningBracket.markdownDescription: **Render collapsed blocks as `{...}`.** The block's real opening bracket is visually hidden and the badge shows `{...}` (or `[...]` / `(...)`) in its place — `function foo() {...}`, exactly like WebStorm. When disabled, a plain `···` badge is shown after the bracket. Only applies while `smartFolding.singleLineFolding` is enabled — with it off, the closing bracket stays visible on its own line, so the opening bracket is shown too and the badge falls back to a plain `···`.

smartFolding.hideNativeFoldPlaceholder.markdownDescription: **Hide VS Code's own `⋯` collapsed-text indicator** that renders to the right of Smart Folding badges. There is no extension API for this, so it is done by setting the `editor.foldPlaceholderForeground` theme color to transparent in your global `workbench.colorCustomizations`. An existing user-set color is never overwritten, and turning this off removes only Smart Folding's own transparent value.

smartFolding.languages.markdownDescription: Language IDs for which the WebStorm-style folding-range provider (single-line folds) is registered. The `···` badge works for every language regardless of this list. Languages whose multiline literals are not yet safely modeled (C, C++, C#, Java, PHP) keep native folding even when listed. Requires a reload after changing.
